articles.title: Day 27: The Semantic Boundaries Between Date, DateTime and Time
articles.excerpt: The order date on a document, the event time on an audit record and the start time on a shift schedule answer different questions. Once they are in a DataSet, though, the first two are both DateTime c…
articles.body: The order date on a document, the event time on an audit record and the start time on a shift schedule answer different questions. Once they are in a DataSet , though, the first two are both DateTime columns and the third is a string column, and the column type alone cannot tell them apart. So what a column is has to be stated separately, by the definition layer. The screen relies on it to pick an editing control, the database relies on it to pick a native type, and when a value travels between client and server, it decides whether a time zone conversion happens (that is the subject of Time Zone Conversion of DateTime ). None of these can be decided from the fact that it is a DateTime alone.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth. Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway. Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010 . Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa.

articles.body: A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage. You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower. articles.title: No more asteroid landing: Engine trouble forces Japan's Hayabusa2 probe to change plans
articles.excerpt: Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 asteroid mission, due to problems with the spacecraft's ion thrusters.
articles.body: Japan's space agency has decided to switch destinations and objectives for the final act of its Hayabusa2 mission, due to the spacecraft suffering trouble with its ion thrusters. The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu . Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end.

articles.title: China rolls out rocket for launch of 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station (video)
articles.excerpt: China has rolled to the launch pad the rocket and spacecraft for its Shenzhou-24 mission, which will fly the first international astronaut to the nation's Tiangong space station.
articles.body: China's space station is set to receive its first foreign astronaut. A Long March 2F rocket, topped with the Shenzhou-24 crew spacecraft, was rolled out to the pad at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, on Tuesday (Nov. 17), with launch expected in the next week. The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026.
